text:
marie-finance: FYI — Devon Harper (consultant) submitted a set of reissued invoices for Jan–Jun saying they incorporated as a UK LTD last month and added a GB VAT ID. Original invoices we received were from a US sole proprietor, no VAT. He sent the PDF: https://invoices.redwood/8792.pdf :thinking_face:

sam-legal: Can you paste the key bits? invoice date vs service period? we need to know if the supplier is asserting the entity change retroactively or only for future work. if retroactive, we need company docs and probably credit notes + reissues. :eyes:

marie-finance: Quick extract from the reissue: ```Invoice #8792-R
Bill to: Redwood Inference
Supplier: Devon Harper Ltd (GB123456789)
Dates: services Jan 01 2026 - Jun 30 2026
Invoice date: 2026-09-12
Amount: EUR 48,000 (VAT 0% - reverse charge claimed)
Reference: original invoice 8590
```

igor-sales: He billed us as US previously, right? sales confirms original PO mapped to 8590 from Feb. If the supplier is now a UK company, VAT treatment depends on place of supply and whether reverse-charge is valid. we also need to be careful about which legal name received the payments historically.

alejandra-ops: If he's asking us to treat past invoices as from the UK entity, we should ask for dated incorporation docs showing effective date <= invoice dates, plus a companies house excerpt and a signed reissued invoice that references the original invoice and a credit note for the original. otherwise we can't change tax treatment retroactively.

sam-legal: Agreed. Checklist I'd need: 1) Companies House doc showing registration and incorporation date; 2) a statement on letterhead explaining the entity change and effective date; 3) reissued invoice referencing original invoice numbers and service periods; 4) proof the VAT number is active (VIES screenshot). If any payments already made, we'll need to treat them as payments to the original entity unless we get valid docs.

emma-payments: Payment for the reissue is scheduled for tomorrow afternoon as part of the supplier run. Please advise whether to hold. currently it's queued as beneficiary: Devon Harper (US) - bank ****234.

marie-finance: Hold payment for 48 hours pending docs. I'll ask Devon to upload Companies House excerpt and a signed credit note + reissue. tell payments not to release to the existing US bank until resolved.

sam-legal: One more tax angle: if we determine the supplier should have been treated as a US person for those past invoices, backup withholding could apply only in certain cases (missing TIN). Gross-up is not standard — we don't gross-up unless contractually agreed. Do not auto-gross-up; we need tax's signoff.

tax-bot: Automated checklist: VALIDATE_VAT->run VIES check; REISSUE->reissued invoice must: reference original invoice, include supplier company reg number & VAT, signed; PAY_HOLD->payments held until documents validated. Additional doc: W-9 if supplier remains US person for earlier periods; W-8BEN-E if now a non-US entity.

igor-sales: also check banking details on reissued invoice (UK company should have GBP/EUR account in its name). if bank name still shows 'Devon Harper' US acct, that's suspicious.

marie-finance: I'll message Devon requesting: (1) Companies House excerpt with incorporation date, (2) signed credit note for 8590, (3) reissued invoice #8792-R referencing 8590 and showing VAT treatment, (4) confirmation of bank account name change / proof. we'll hold the run.

alejandra-ops: If he refuses or can't provide retro docs, we instruct him to issue a new invoice for future work under the UK entity and leave prior invoices as paid/owed to the US person. escalate to legal if he pushes for retroactive VAT recovery.

emma-payments: Holding now. I'll flag the payment run and remove the item from processing queue. :white_check_mark:

marie-finance: Thanks — I'll update once Devon uploads docs. tagging @sam-legal and @tax-bot for review when available.

sam-legal: Thanks. If docs look clean and the VAT is valid we can apply reverse-charge going forward, but retro changes need the credit note + documentary proof. No gross-up without a contractual clause.

marie-finance: Noted. closing loop here — expect first update in 24h.
